title: Jest cannot reproduce strict-mode lodash crashes; test the property assignment directly
answers: why does my jest test not reproduce the rspack cloneDeep error
how to test getter-only property failures in strict mode
body:
Jest transforms lodash to CommonJS, which is not strict, so `cloneDeep` silently ignores writes to getter-only properties in tests. The production Rspack/ESM build throws on the same writes.
To cover a fix like this, reproduce what lodash does directly. Create `Object.create(Klass.prototype)`, assign the property (for example `clone.length = 3`), and assert it does not throw. Test files are ES modules transpiled with class semantics, so the assignment throws there when no setter exists.
Example: the 'Cloning DataFrame' describe block in packages/grafana-data/src/dataframe/MutableDataFrame.test.ts.
applies: Writing Jest tests for bugs that only show up in strict-mode/ESM (Rspack) bundles
